title: Embercliff - retail LLM friction log
content:
Call: Embercliff integration kickoff (03/09)
Attendees: Priya (RD), Marco (CS), Lena (Sales Eng), Tom B. (Embercliff engineering), Aisha R. (Embercliff product)

Quick summary:
- Customer: Embercliff (regional chain ~120 stores). Pilot: returns-assistant + POS product lookup for floor agents + post-purchase email summarization.
- Primary ask: low-latency responses at POS (goal: <300ms tail for agent UI), and privacy for PII/transaction tokens -> leaning Private (VPC) + HSM for keying.
- Secondary: embeddings search for product catalog (monthly index updates), want near real-time SKU additions during sale events.

Notes / requirements captured:
- Traffic profile:
  - Peak in-store concurrency: ~180 agents during peak (holiday), expected pilot traffic 30–50 rps initially, scale target 200 rps.
  - Typical prompt sizes: 50–400 tokens. Post-purchase summarization jobs can be 2–5k tokens (batch offline is OK).
  - Embedding queries: high QPS for product lookup during checkout (embedding vector store will be separate; they want caching + fallback to exact SKU match).

- Security / compliance:
  - PCI scope: they cannot send full PANs to hosted API. Need strict redaction client-side and tokenization before anything touches Redwood endpoints.
  - They require KMS/HSM integration (AWS KMS cross-account) and audit logs retention 12+ months.
  - Data residency: primary region us-east-1, must support aurora replica in us-east-2 for DR.

- Deployment form factor:
  - Preference: Private (VPC) with customer-managed peering. Consider Dedicated if HSM integration becomes blocking.
  - Ops constraint: Embercliff runs strict egress policies; need IP allowlist (we'll provide static egress ranges for the control plane) and option for air-gapped sync of model artifacts.

Technical gotchas called out on call (urgent)
1) Cold-start latency for large models: their UI requires <300ms tail for short prompts; large-model cold starts will violate. Options: keep warm pool on dedicated GPUs or use smaller quantized variants for POS routes.
2) SKU normalization: product titles are messy; embeddings require canonicalization pre-processing. Suggested pipeline: client-side SKU canonicalizer -> hashed SKU id -> embedding lookup. Avoid sending raw customer text for mapping to reduce PII.
3) Prefix caching + cache invalidation: during flash sales inventory changes often; cache TTL needs to be short or invalidation hook required. Discuss webhook from their catalog system.
4) Cost sensitivity: they want predictable per-store pricing. Recommend reserved capacity for pilot month and autoscaling caps to avoid runaway token spend.

Integration specifics (engineering follow-up items):
- API contract for POS flow (Tom to share sample JSON): expected fields: store_id, agent_id (hashed), session_id, prompt_template_id, sanitized_text. Must confirm whether agent audio -> speech->text happens client-side.
- Embedding pipeline: schedule nightly index + hot-update API for ~1000 SKUs/day during promos. Need recommended vector dimensionality (recommend 1536 / ada-like) and storage options (we suggested Pinecone/redis-vec/PG vector + caching).
- Rollback & fallback: define fallback policy in Redwood Console to smaller model variant (reduce filter complexity) when latency SLO breached. Also fallback to last-known-answer for embedding misses.

Prompting /品質 notes (raw):
- POS prompt must include a strict instruction to ask 2 clarifying Qs max (to avoid long interactions) and to return structured JSON with fields: action, primary_sku_id, alt_skus[], reason.
- Example small prompt (for engineer copy): "You are an in-store assistant. Given sanitized customer text and store inventory, return primary_sku and up to 3 alternatives, confidence 0-1. Keep answer <=40 tokens." 

Outstanding questions for Embercliff (to resolve on next call):
- Will they accept partial de-identification (hashing) of customer identifiers or need full tokenization before anything leaves their network?
- Which catalog system (A) does Embercliff use? (Tom said custom Postgres + data-lake sync) -> need DB schema export for SKU mapping.
- Durability SLA requirement for embeddings index updates (do they need transactional guarantees?)

Action items (owner, target):
- Tom: share sample POS JSON + data dictionary (due 2026-03-14)
- Marco: prepare Private deployment checklist + network diagram for peering (due 2026-03-16)
- Priya: draft cost projection for 50/100/200 rps with reserved vs hosted options; include token estimate for typical session (due 2026-03-15)
- Lena: schedule technical deep-dive with SRE and product next week; include SRE checklist for HSM integration (due -> schedule by 2026-03-13)
- Eng: propose small-model variant (gpt-small-quant?) latency benchmark (initial numbers by 2026-03-18)

Risks / mitigation
- Risk: Cold-starts break UX during peak. Mitigation: warm pool + prioritized routing for POS routes; use shorter context models.
- Risk: Catalog drift causes embedding misses. Mitigation: webhook invalidation + hot-update API + TTL 30s on hot paths.
- Risk: PCI scope explosion if tokens leak. Mitigation: client SDK for redaction + mandatory PKI step, engineering checklist enforced in onboarding.

Notes to self / internal talking points for next call
- Push the idea of a hybrid approach: Private control plane + Dedicated inference nodes for POS to get both security and warm-pools. We can later migrate to full Private if they want.
- Emphasize cost predictability (reserved capacity) and show tradeoffs: reserve = lower unit cost, but operational burden for autoscale during promos.
- Ask SRE about support window for in-region warm-pools during peak holiday + pre-warm script.

Misc quick snippets from call
- "If it hits slow even once, the floor agents will avoid using it" — Aisha
- They have a compliance checklist that requires sample audit logs before pilot sign-off.

Next meeting: technical deep-dive (SRE + Embergcliff infra) proposed 2026-03-17 16:00 ET. Confirm attendees and pre-reads: network diagram, POS JSON, compliance checklist.

-- end of scratchpad (keep informal)
